_comment: Replace the agenda / questions / email fields with the VERBATIM output of the B1 workflow from thesis_meeting_prep_prototype.ipynb. Do not edit the model's wording. Set "generated": true and fill "run" once you do. Anything still false renders as a visible placeholder on the page.

scenarios.title: Early stage
scenarios.subtitle: Scope not settled
scenarios.situation: First supervisor meeting after the topic was provisionally accepted. Has read widely, written nothing. Suspects the topic is too broad but cannot say why.
scenarios.note:
meeting thurs 30 min

ok so topic is "AI in education" but my supervisor said last time it was
too broad?? I dont really get what too broad means here. I have like 20
papers saved. Some are about chatbots for language learning, some about
grading automation, two about accessibility.

should I pick just one? or is there a way to keep it broad
also do I need a research question already at this stage or does that
come later

I don't want to waste her time with stupid questions
scenarios.tests: The "should I pick just one" question is the substituted-judgement trap. "Do I need a research question at this stage" is an institutional question hiding inside an academic one.

scenarios.title: Mid thesis
scenarios.subtitle: The method is not working
scenarios.situation: Six weeks in. The planned method has run into a wall. Wants to change approach but is worried about how that will be received.
scenarios.note:
20 min slot monday

the survey isn't working. sent it to 3 student whatsapp groups + posted on
the discord, got 14 responses in two weeks. I planned for 80+. at 14 I
can't really say anything statistically.

options I see:
- keep waiting (but I lose 3-4 weeks)
- switch to interviews, maybe 6-8 people
- change the whole RQ to something that doesn't need a survey

I think interviews but that changes my whole methods chapter which is
already written and she approved it. is that a problem? will it look like
I didn't plan properly

also need to know if the methods chapter change needs re-approval or if I
just do it
scenarios.tests: A real decision with trade-offs, plus an emotional undercurrent the toolkit should not coach on. "Does the methods change need re-approval" is the clearest institutional test.

scenarios.title: Late stage
scenarios.subtitle: Behind schedule
scenarios.situation: Eight weeks from submission, roughly three weeks behind. Needs to renegotiate scope or timeline and has been avoiding the conversation.
scenarios.note:
need to talk to her about the timeline, been putting this off

where I am: ch 1,2,3 done (draft). ch 4 results - half. ch 5 discussion -
nothing. conclusion nothing.
was supposed to have ch4 finished 2 weeks ago.

reasons: the data cleaning took way longer than I thought, and I was sick
for a week in october.

what I want to ask:
- can I drop the second case study? it was always "if time permits" but
  it's in my proposal
- is an extension possible and what do I need for it
- if I submit ch4 next week can she read it before the end

honestly I also just want to know if she thinks I'm going to make it
scenarios.tests: Two explicit procedural questions plus a request for reassurance that is not the toolkit's to give. "Can I drop the second case study" is a scope decision belonging to the supervisor.
